actions.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 414 - 2 (Roll no. 227).
Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by the Yeas and Nays: (2/3 required): 414 - 2 (Roll no. 227).
Considered as unfinished business. (consideration: CR H4251-4252)

At the conclusion of debate, the chair put the question on the motion to suspend the rules. Mr. Hill (AR) objected to the vote on the grounds that a quorum was not present. Further proceedings on the motion were postponed. The point of no quorum was considered as withdrawn.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 2478.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H4222-4226; text: CR H4222-4223)
Mr. Hill (AR) moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended.
Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 313.
Reported (Amended) by the Committee on Financial Services. H. Rept. 119-361.
Reported (Amended) by the Committee on Financial Services. H. Rept. 119-361.
Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 50 - 0.
Committee Consideration and Mark-up Session Held
Referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.

committees.name: Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee

dimensions.assessment: Affects open-end investment companies, transfer agents, security holders age 65 or older, and individuals age 18 or older with mental or physical impairments.
dimensions.evidence: an individual (1) age 65 or older, or (2) age 18 or older who is unable to protect his or her own interests

dimensions.assessment: Allows temporary delays in securities redemptions for up to 15 or 25 business days in suspected exploitation cases, which directly affects access to funds during that period.
dimensions.evidence: postpone the date of payment or satisfaction upon redemption of any redeemable security... for a period of not more than 15 business days.

dimensions.assessment: No significant direct federal spending or revenue changes are stated, though the SEC is directed to submit a report and consult with various financial agencies.
Amends the Investment Company Act of 1940 to add specific procedural requirements, record-keeping, notifications, and internal company procedures for financial institutions.
dimensions.evidence: Section 22 of the Investment Company Act of 1940 (15 U.S.C. 80a-22) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory amendment to securities law with ongoing procedural and reporting requirements.

missing_information: Exact number of individuals or accounts that will experience delayed redemptions
Specific cost estimates for the SEC and participating financial institutions
importance_detail.rationale: The bill creates procedures for investment companies and transfer agents to delay redemptions of securities when financial exploitation of specified adults is suspected, impacting older individuals and those with impairments, and requires reports from the SEC.
